title: Luring the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Out of a Cave with Music; Death of the Fire God
medium: Hanging scroll, ink and color on paper
subject: Amaterasu, Iwato (heavenly rock-cave), Ame-no-Uzume
description: The kami perform music and dance at the cave mouth to lure the Sun Goddess Amaterasu back out after her retreat into the Iwato, which plunged the world into darkness. A celebrated Edo-period depiction of the Iwato myth.
attribution: Metropolitan Museum of Art (Met Open Access, public domain)

title: Amaterasu Emerging from the Cave (Origin of the Iwato Kagura)
subject: Amaterasu, Iwato, kagura dance
description: Kunisada's large print of Amaterasu emerging from the rock-cave — the moment that gave rise to the Iwato-kagura ritual dances performed at shrines to this day.
attribution: Utagawa Kunisada (d. 1865); public domain
